## toon.ts (2807 lines)

Our own flat 2D cartoon cast (riflemen, officer, townsfolk, kid, parent) + 2D effects, drawn on a canvas. Construction v2 (characters.md, our own cast): superellipse heads (pointed crown 1.75 / full jaw 2.3, chin taper, seeded side bulge + tilt), bean torsos, single-stroke limbs with ink-dot hands, a thick-thin plum outline weighted away from the light, soft painted crescents, deadpan lidded eyes, no blush, no catchlights. Design space 600 x 1000 units (soles at y = 975); the canvas transform scales it.

```ts
type Outfit = {
  jacket: string; pants: string; boots: string; hat?: string | null; /** "khan" headscarf: depth of the peak over the forehead, 1 = the classic V (default), 0 = a flat soft band (the V reads as a scowl in close-up) */ khanPeak?: number; belt?: string | null; buttons?: string; rifle?: boolean;
  sash?: string; sword?: boolean; moustache?: string; skin?: string; head?: number; cap?: string; hair?: string; dress?: string;
  build?: Build;
  /** wet hair strands over the face (drowned) */ wet?: boolean;
  /** wrinkles (grandmother) */ old?: boolean;
  /** glasses frame colour (octagonal metal frames) */ glasses?: string;
  /** brow thickness multiplier (1 = default) */ brows?: number;
  /** quilted puffer jacket (stitch lines + zip, no buttons); collar = colour of the tee showing at the neck */ puffer?: boolean; collar?: string;
  /** jaw exponent override: higher = fuller, rounder lower face (default ~2.3) */ jaw?: number;
  // ---- Cây gạo (14th-century cast) ----
  /** `dress` = colour of an ankle-length skirt (váy) under the tunic. `head` = head-shape seed: overrides the caller's
   *  seed for the head contour only, so a character keeps one face whatever index the stage gives it. */
  /** cross-collar tunic (áo giao lĩnh): colour of the collar band; no buttons */ cross?: string;
  /** feminine face: lash flick at the outer eye corners, a hint of red lips (colour), narrower jaw */ fem?: boolean; lips?: string;
  /** long robe to the feet in the jacket colour, with wide sleeves (Taoist) */ robe?: boolean;
  /** long thin beard colour */ beard?: string;
  /** ill: dark under-eyes, a few loose strands of hair */ sick?: boolean;
  /** clay figurine: painted dot eyes + painted mouth (expression and blinks ignored), hairline cracks, stiff */ clay?: boolean;
  /** ghost hair: longer, ragged hem, a strand over one eye (with hat "silk") */ messy?: boolean;
  // ---- Ma da (long): acting cast ----
  /** whole-figure scale about the soles (1 = default): a small child next to adults, e.g. 0.8 */ small?: number;
  /** torso width multiplier (1 = default): a thin old man ~0.88 */ slim?: number;
};
```

```ts
type FrontOpts = {
  phase?: number; expr?: Expr; mode?: "march" | "stroll" | "stand" | "sit" | "fall"; look?: number; blink?: boolean | number; lift?: number;
  prop?: Prop; tilt?: number; headTilt?: number; wave?: number;
  /** canvas angle the key light comes FROM (painted crescent + thick outline side) */
  light?: number; facing?: -1 | 0 | 1; seed?: number;
  // ---- opt-in acting (all default to the old drawing) ----
  /** arm pose [name, k, side?]: blended from the current arms by k in 0..1 (animate k). side -1 | 1 picks the arm of the
   *  one-armed gestures (default: the facing side, else 1; the other arm if that one holds a prop). Modes stand / sit /
   *  stroll / march; ignored in "fall" and with a two-handed prop (lute, rope, cup, kite). An arm holding a prop keeps it. */
  gesture?: [Gesture, number, (-1 | 1)?];
  /** mouth openness 0..1 over the expression's own mouth (0 = unchanged): flap it on the syllables of speech */
  talk?: number;
  /** seen from behind: no face, the hair / hat covers the back of the head, plain back of the jacket (stand / sit / stroll) */
  back?: boolean;
  /** breathing -1..1: the chest and shoulders rise, the head lifts about 1 % of the card (drive it with a sine) */
  breath?: number;
  /** pupil offset [x, y] in -1..1 (continuous; x replaces `look`) */
  gaze?: [number, number];
};
```

};

## grade.ts (208 lines)

Colour grade for the bridge short (post agent): references/grade/GradeEffect.ts (reports/grade.md) verbatim, plus GRADES / GRADE_STRENGTH / gradeFor() so the lead can re-fit the presets after the lighting merge. The presets were fitted to the OLD unlit stills: after the WORLD lighting lands they will over-correct; re-fit (grade.md 5.C) or lower GRADE_STRENGTH. Each Inner (crossfade layer) grades with its own shot's light, so the DOM crossfade at XFADE frames (shots 10->11, 13->14) cross-fades the presets as well. GradeEffect: the fitted reference-style colour grade as a postprocessing 6.37 Effect. Put it LAST in the EffectComposer, after ToneMappingEffect. It works on display-referred values: the input (linear, already tone-mapped to 0..1) is encoded to sRGB, graded exactly like scripts/grade.py (validated on our stills), and decoded back to linear for the composer's output encoding. 1. RGB tone curve: monotone cubic Hermite through 7 knots at x = 0, .1, .25, .5, .75, .9, 1 2. saturation around luma Y' (Rec.709 weights on the encoded values), separately for shadows / mids / highlights 3. 3-way tint (split tone): zero-luma RGB offsets in shadows, mids, highlights 4. vignette: x (1 - k * smoothstep(r0, 1, r)), r = elliptical radius, corners = 1 `amount` blends the whole grade (0 = bypass) so it can be dialled back once lighting/albedo work brightens the render.

## cardshade.ts (86 lines)

Character card shading (lighting.md 9.2 / 9.5). Replaces the flat emissive "pasted-on" look: the card takes the scene light colour as a tint, keeps a bright floor where a cast shadow falls on it (charShade ~.86), and gets a soft side gradient toward the real sun (head ~charGrad, torso ~bodyGrad) with a lavender far side. Contract with WORLD: LFB (sun shadow visibility inside three's light loop) and CHAR (uniforms world.ts updates from LIGHTS every frame) come from shade.ts; the sun direction is three's own directional light 0. The drawing already carries a painted crescent (toon.ts shadedFill / gradFill), so the shader adds GRAD_K of the preset gradient, and the preset tint (measured on WHITE heads) is applied at TINT_K so peach skin stays clean (lighting.md 9.1 note: golden ~[1, .88, .76], day ~[1, .97, .96] for peach skin).

## ink.ts (394 lines)

Ink outlines for the 3D world, matched to the reference measurements (references/reports/outlines.md recipe, post-agent changes: widths scale with the output height (pxScale = height / 1920, so 5.1 px at 1080x1920 is 6.8 px at 1440x2560), RMAX 9 for headroom at 1440, fog-tinted ink (scene.fog, x0.3), `noInkFallback` below. Round 2: widths x1.5 (5.1 -> 3.3 px from 6 to 90 m), pure near-black #030303, far opacity 0.95, depth jumps from 1 %.  How it works 1. Re-render the WORLD ONLY (camera layer 0) into a non-MSAA target: view-space normal (rgb), coverage (a) and a depth texture. Character billboards, effect cards, sky, clouds and smoke live on layer NOINK, so they never get rectangle outlines and never cut holes into the world's lines. 2. Edge mask (full resolution), pixel steps 1..6 along x, y and both diagonals: depth  - signed 2nd difference of 1/z (exactly 0 on any plane, so no grazing-angle false lines) -> only the NEAR side of a depth jump is inked, as a band `width` px wide (silhouettes vs sky, object vs object, thin ropes become solid lines like the reference); crease - normal angle > ~50 deg to a neighbour at the same depth, two-sided band ~0.64*width px wide, concave folds (object meets ground, inner corners) at 0.7 strength; coverage is continuous in the width (no width popping when the camera moves), width shrinks a little with distance (3.4 px at 6 m -> 2.2 px at 90 m, log-distance), opacity to 0.75, fades out by 450 m; no ink where the main depth buffer has something nearer than the world (characters / cards in front). 3. Composite: 3x3 tent-filtered mask (anti-aliasing), near-black ink blended in display gamma (like Canvas2D), written back into the input buffer (colour only; the composer's depth texture stays intact). This is a Pass (not an Effect), so R3F's <EffectComposer> keeps it as its own pass BEFORE the merged DOF + Bloom + ToneMapping EffectPass: the depth of field then blurs the lines together with the background. Verified in a toy scene with this exact stack (MSAA 4, HalfFloat, DOF/Bloom/Neutral): compiles, no GL errors, measured EW 3.7 / 3.2 / 2.6 / 1.5 / 1.1 px at 3 / 12 / 25 / 90 / 200 m (silhouettes) and 2.3 -> 0.9 px (creases).

- `const NOINK` (line 29): Layer for things that must never be outlined (camera-facing sprites, sky, clouds, smoke).
- `type InkOptions` (line 31)

```ts
type InkOptions = {
  color?: THREE.ColorRepresentation; // sRGB hex of the ink
  strength?: number; // max opacity
  widthNear?: number; // silhouette / depth-jump line width in px at distNear (1080x1920 output)
  widthFar?: number; // ... at distFar
  distNear?: number; // m
  distFar?: number; // m
  creaseScale?: number; // crease line width / silhouette line width
  depthLo?: number; // relative depth jump (1 - z_near / z_far) where lines start
  depthHi?: number; // ... where they are full strength
  angleLo?: number; // crease angle (deg) where lines start
  angleHi?: number; // ... where they are full strength
  concaveGain?: number; // strength of concave folds (object meets ground, inner corners)
  farOpacity?: number; // opacity multiplier reached at distFar
  fadeNear?: number; // m: start of the far fade-out
  fadeFar?: number; // m: lines gone
};
```

## lensblur.ts (140 lines)

Thin-lens depth of field for the reference's soft backgrounds (reports/depth.md 6.1), as two deterministic gather passes. CoC radius (px at 1080x1920) = cInf * |1 - focus / depth|, x nearScale in front of the focus plane, clamped to maxCoC. Every pixel size is multiplied in the shader by (output height / 1920), so the picture is the same at 540, 1080 and 1440 widths. pre  : 16-tap gather over 0.29 x the CoC. It fills the gaps between the main taps, so the composite kernel is a smooth disc (1024 effective taps) instead of 64 visible copies of every edge. main : 64-tap Vogel disc over 0.96 x the CoC (pre + main together = a disc of sigma CoC/2), plus a 32-tap near field gather that lets a blurred foreground spread over sharper pixels behind it. Occlusion rules (no halos, no dark rims): a sample counts only if its own CoC reaches this pixel, a farther sample may never spread wider than this pixel's own CoC (sharp subjects keep clean silhouettes), and the result is renormalised by the accepted weights. Fixed sample pattern, no per-pixel noise: no grain, no frame-to-frame flicker. Both passes are CONVOLUTION effects, so R3F's <EffectComposer> gives each its own EffectPass.

- `class LensBlurEffect extends Effect` (line 74)
- `class LensBlur` (line 94): The pair of passes the composer needs (pre first, then main); set focus / cInf once per frame on this object.
**film grain (end of the chain, after the grade)**

- `class GrainEffect extends Effect` (line 130)
